question: Can online RL (PPO) after a short SFT warm-up, using only final-answer correctness as reward on the same training questions, give better math-reasoning generalisation than SFT on one annotated CoT per question?
hypothesis: Learning from many sampled reasoning paths per question, rather than a single annotated path, generalises better than SFT.
contributions: Introduce ReFT: SFT warm-up then PPO with rewards derived from ground-truth answers, on the same data as SFT.
Experiments with CodeLLaMA and Galactica on GSM8K, MathQA and SVAMP, natural-language and program CoT.
ReFT benefits further from majority voting and reward-model reranking at inference.

method.summary: Two stages: SFT warm-up for 1-2 epochs (more on MathQA), then PPO with a shared linear value head, reward 1 for correct extracted answer (0.1 partial for a numeric wrong answer on numeric datasets, 0 otherwise) plus a KL penalty to the warm-up policy. Compared with SFT, offline self-training and online self-training on the same questions; also combined with voting and RM reranking.
method.task: math word-problem solving with chain-of-thought (natural-language N-CoT and Python program P-CoT)

datasets.name: GSM8K
datasets.source: Cobbe et al. 2021a; CoT annotations from few-shot GPT-3.5-turbo following Jie et al. 2023
datasets.preprocessing: program CoT is a Python function with docstring repeating the question

datasets.name: MathQA numeric
datasets.source: Jie and Lu 2023 variant with options removed

other.note: Table 2 prints size as 0.7B; text says 7B

models.name: Reward model for reranking
models.architecture: LM with linear classifier on last-token hidden state

other.training: 3 epochs, batch 24, max length 700, linear schedule, 10% warm-up, max lr 1e-6; data: 100 sampled CoTs per training question from warm-up model, deduplicated, binary labels

training.objective: Warm-up: token-level SFT cross-entropy (Eq 1). RL: PPO clipped policy loss + alpha * clipped value loss (Eq 2), reward 1 / 0.1 / 0 minus beta*KL to warm-up policy, GAE advantages
training.lr: warm-up 1e-5; RL 3e-7 (7B models); small models RL 3e-6 and SFT 2e-5
training.warmup: 10% warm-up ratio for the optimiser; SFT warm-up epochs: 2 (GSM8K, SVAMP, MathQA P-CoT), 5 (MathQA MCQ N-CoT), 10 (MathQA numeric); small models 10 epochs (Galactica-125M, Codegen-350M on GSM8K/SVAMP), 40 on MathQA MCQ, Codeparrot-small 40 on all
training.epochs: RL 300 epochs (7B); small models 700 RL epochs; SFT baseline 40 epochs (100 for small models on MathQA MCQ), best checkpoint chosen; Offline-ST 20 epochs
training.seq_len: max length 1024 (warm-up/SFT); RL max question length 300, max sampling length 700
training.hardware: 8x A100-80GB, DeepSpeed ZeRO stage 2, HuggingFace Accelerate

other.ppo: lambda 1, gamma 0.95, alpha 5, epsilon 0.2, U (updates per RL step) 2; alpha 5/1/0.1 for Galactica-125M/Codeparrot-small/Codegen-350M
other.value_model: linear value head on policy last hidden states (shared)
other.partial_reward: 0.1 for extractable numeric but wrong answer, numeric datasets only

inference.decoding: sampling for voting/reranking and baseline data; greedy for accuracy inferred: Table 2 reports single value accuracy but decoding not stated
inference.samples: 100 CoTs per question for majority voting and reranking; 100 CoTs per training question for Offline-ST (then 10 random unique correct kept); single run per cell, no seeds stated
inference.prompting: few-shot GPT-3.5-turbo prompting only to create annotations (following Jie et al. 2023)

metrics.name: value accuracy
metrics.definition: extracted final answer equals ground truth (GSM8K, SVAMP numeric; MathQA option letter)

metrics.name: human qualitative score
metrics.definition: 4 annotators score logic, naming, compactness each 0-1 on 50 GSM8K test questions all three models solve; overall = sum, max 3

baselines: Online self-training (same warm-up, SFT on correct samples + gold)
WizardMath, MathCoder, MAmmoTH-Coder, DeepSeekMath, GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4 (reported numbers, Table 4)
eval.protocol: Single run per cell as far as stated; no seeds, intervals or significance tests. Voting: majority valid answer among 100 samples; reranking: highest RM score.

limits: ReFT needs many more epochs than SFT to converge (Fig 4b); a larger lr risks instability and collapse, a larger batch costs compute. No wall-clock, GPU-hour or token budget is given.

Reward depends only on the final answer, so it is hackable when the answer space is small (MathQA MCQ A-E); a wrong chain that picks the right letter gets reward 1. Process rewards are suggested for future work.
ReFT needs an SFT warm-up; a warm-up-free method is future work. Only PPO was used; DPO/IPO were tried briefly.
No seeds, intervals or significance tests; all table cells appear to be single runs. Decoding for Table 2 evaluation not stated.
Only math word problems; annotations come from GPT-3.5-turbo. Comparison rows in Table 4 are copied from other papers with different data sizes.
Gemma preliminary results were dropped for unresolved implementation issues (footnote 7).
